rewrites.text: Redwood City grew from a lumber port on Redwood Creek, the waterway that Gold Rush loggers used to float redwood timber down to San Francisco Bay. The city incorporated in 1867 and has been the county seat of San Mateo County since the county formed in 1856. Its slogan, 'Climate Best by Government Test,' dates to a national climate survey that put Redwood City on the map. Families here deliver at Sequoia Hospital, a Dignity Health facility with a Level II NICU staffed by Lucile Packard Children's Hospital Stanford neonatologists, or at Kaiser Permanente Redwood City Medical Center, a CMS Birthing-Friendly hospital with a Level II nursery. California's Medi-Cal program covers doula services statewide.

Redwood City families deliver at Sequoia Hospital, a Dignity Health facility featuring a Family Birth Center with a Level II NICU staffed by Lucile Packard Children's Hospital Stanford neonatologists, or at Kaiser Permanente Redwood City Medical Center with a Level II nursery. Sequoia Hospital has earned a 5th consecutive 'A' Hospital Safety Grade from The Leapfrog Group and is a Blue Shield of California Blue Distinction Center for Maternity Care. Kaiser Permanente Redwood City is a CMS Birthing-Friendly facility. Both hospitals serve the Redwood City community with comprehensive maternity care.

Sequoia Hospital in Redwood City is a Dignity Health facility and the primary maternity hospital for the city. The Family Birth Center features private LDR rooms and a six-bed Level II NICU staffed by Lucile Packard Children's Hospital Stanford neonatologists, who are nationally recognized by U.S. News & World Report. The hospital has certified nurse-midwives on staff, 24/7 OB hospitalists, and follows a family-centered care model with couplet care so mother and baby remain together. Sequoia is a Blue Shield of California Blue Distinction Center for Maternity Care and has earned a 5th consecutive 'A' Hospital Safety Grade from The Leapfrog Group. Doulas are welcome as support persons. The hospital played a role in rebuilding San Francisco after the 1906 earthquake, as lumber moved through the Port of Redwood City to reconstruct the city.

rewrites.text: Kaiser Permanente Redwood City Medical Center offers labor and delivery services with a Level II nursery for newborns needing extra care. The hospital is a CMS Birthing-Friendly facility, a designation from the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services recognizing a commitment to high-quality maternity care. It features private birthing suites, 24/7 anesthesia coverage, and certified nurse-midwives on staff. Doulas are welcome as support persons. The hospital accepts Medi-Cal and most major insurance plans. Language interpretation services are available. Located at 1100 Veterans Blvd, the facility serves Redwood City and the surrounding Peninsula communities.

California licenses Licensed Midwives (LMs) and Certified Nurse-Midwives (CNMs), with LMs attending home births and CNMs practicing in hospitals. Redwood City families have access to hospital-based midwifery at Sequoia Hospital and Kaiser Permanente Redwood City Medical Center, plus home-birth midwives serving the wider San Mateo County area. The city's identity as a port town on Redwood Creek and the San Francisco Bay gives it a distinct working-waterfront character compared to the academic-med-center pull of Palo Alto to the south and the larger Peninsula health systems to the north. California's Medi-Cal program covers doula services statewide, and the state's Licensed Midwife (LM) credential is among the most established in the country for out-of-hospital birth.

newFAQs.q: What is Redwood City known for besides birth care?
newFAQs.a: Redwood City is the county seat of San Mateo County and grew from a lumber port on Redwood Creek during the Gold Rush era. Its slogan, 'Climate Best by Government Test,' reflects a national climate survey. The Port of Redwood City is the only deepwater port on San Francisco Bay south of San Francisco, and the city played a role in rebuilding San Francisco after the 1906 earthquake. Downtown Broadway features a pedestrian mall with an Entertainment Zone pilot launched in 2026.

newFAQs.q: How does Sequoia Hospital compare to hospitals in Palo Alto and San Mateo?
newFAQs.a: Sequoia Hospital is a community hospital in Redwood City operated by Dignity Health, with a Level II NICU staffed by Lucile Packard Children's Hospital Stanford neonatologists. Unlike Palo Alto's Lucile Packard Children's Hospital Stanford, which is a Level IV academic medical center, Sequoia is a community facility focused on family-centered care with couplet care. Compared to San Mateo Medical Center, Sequoia offers private LDR rooms and a Blue Distinction Center for Maternity Care designation. Families in Redwood City have a community hospital option that bridges the gap between the academic medical pull of Stanford to the south and the larger Peninsula systems to the north.

newFAQs.q: What is the Port of Redwood City's connection to the city's birth care community?
newFAQs.a: The Port of Redwood City is the only deepwater port on San Francisco Bay south of San Francisco, and it shaped Redwood City's identity as a working waterfront town. The port was pivotal in rebuilding San Francisco after the 1906 earthquake, with lumber moved through the port to reconstruct the city. Today, Redwood City's waterfront character and Bayfront location give it a distinct sense of place compared to inland Peninsula cities. This port heritage is part of what makes Redwood City's community feel different from the academic-med-center identity of Palo Alto or the county-seat-of-healthcare identity of San Mateo.
